name: Soviet Union (USSR) 1922-1939
lenguages: Russian (and national languages of the republics)
description: The USSR was founded in 1922 following the Bolshevik victory in the Civil War. During World War II, on September 17 1939 it invaded eastern Poland. This expansion was enabled by the secret protocol of the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact with Nazi Germany, which defined spheres of influence in Eastern Europe, allowing Stalin to annex territories to create a strategic buffer and reclaim former imperial lands.

name: Soviet Union (USSR) 1945-1991
lenguages: Russian (official lingua franca) and national languages of the Soviet republics
description: After its victory in World War II, the USSR emerged as a superpower and consolidated its borders by incorporating the Baltic states, securing Poland’s frontier along the Curzon Line, annexing territories such as Kaliningrad, and establishing a socialist bloc in Eastern Europe as a strategic buffer. During the Cold War it rivaled the United States, but economic decline and political reforms weakened central control. Between 1989 and 1991, its republics declared independence, and the union formally dissolved on December 25, 1991.

name: Greenland
GovernmentType: Autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark
description: After centuries of Norse and Danish-Norwegian presence, Greenland became a formal Danish colony in 1814. In 1953, its status changed from colony to a constitutional district. Seeking greater self-determination, Greenland achieved Home Rule in 1979 and expanded Self-Government in 2009. Today, it is an autonomous nation within the Kingdom of Denmark, managing most internal affairs independently while relying on Denmark for defense and foreign policy. Though it possesses the legal right to pursue full independence, it remains economically linked to the Danish realm.
